newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico's crude ports opened due to better weather.
newsitem.headline: Mexico's crude ports opened due to better weather.

text.p: Mexico crude ports Pajaritos in Veracruz state and Dos Bocas in Tabasco state reopened early Wednesday as waves and winds relaxed, port authorities said.
The ports reopened at 0800 local/1400 GMT.
Pajaritos had been closed since late Monday and Dos Bocas had been closed since early Tuesday.

The control tower captain at Pajaritos, Eduardo Lopez, told Reuters that waves were just two feet high and wind speeds had relaxed. At Dos Bocas, a port official who declined to be named said waves were still eight feet high, but winds had relaxed.
The third and largest of Mexico's crude ports, Cayo Arcas in Campeche state, remained open during a cold front hovering over the Gulf of Mexico.

Cayo Arcas ships an average 611,000 barrels per day (bpd) of crude, Dos Bocas ships 440,000 bpd and Pajaritos ships 399,000 bpd, according to the latest figures from Mexico's oil and gas monopoly Petroleos Mexicanos (Pemex).
